title: Multi-modal Longitudinal Representation Learning for Predicting Neoadjuvant Therapy Response in Breast Cancer Treatment
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This study addresses prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer using longitudinal imaging rather than single-time-point analysis. Its goal is to learn therapy-response signals from serial breast DCE-MRI and paired radiology reports without relying on dense tumor segmentation labels. The main novelty is the MLRL temporal foundation model, which combines single-time vision-text alignment with multi-time temporal visual and textual progress learning, plus cross-modal temporal consistency constraints to handle heterogeneous response trajectories across patients. Unlike prior vision-language or longitudinal self-supervised methods, it explicitly models change between timepoints and produces interpretable progression maps aligned with report language. The main takeaway is that this longitudinal multimodal self-supervised approach improved pCR prediction, label efficiency, and temporal interpretability on both internal and external cohorts.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Netherlands Cancer Institute in-house longitudinal breast MRI + paired radiology reports (private; 3,719 scans from 1,420 patients for pretraining; downstream subset 1,091 patients with paired pre/post exams); I-SPY2 longitudinal DCE-MRI cohort (public; 572 patients, 2,516 exams after exclusions, used for downstream external evaluation)
Baseline model/architecture: Main model: MLRL temporal foundation model with ResNet-50 image encoder + ClinicalBERT text encoder, temporal visual progress (TVP) / temporal textual progress (TTP) modules, and MLP late-fusion classifier; key comparators: ImageNet+ClinicalBERT, GLoRIA, REFERS, LNE, MLDRL, MLF
Training Approach: Two-stage training: self-supervised multimodal longitudinal pretraining on paired MRI/report timepoints using single-time vision-text alignment (InfoNCE), multi-time temporal visual/textual progress learning (TVP/TTP), and cross-modal temporal consistency losses; followed by supervised fine-tuning with binary cross-entropy for pCR prediction in zero-shot, few-shot (5%, 10%), and full-shot settings
Medical Phase (pre/post): both (pre-NAT plus mid/post-NAT during treatment; pre-surgical)
Medical Modality: Multi-modal (longitudinal breast DCE-MRI + radiology reports; histopathologic pCR used as outcome label)
Model input modality: image+text (paired prior/current maximum-intensity-projection DCE-MRI images plus paired reports when available)
Evaluation Metric & corresponding value: Main cohort comparison (Table I): Internal validation—AUROC=0.843 (95% CI 0.806-0.876), Sensitivity=0.819 (0.749-0.882), Specificity=0.769 (0.697-0.833), PPV=0.634 (0.553-0.713), NPV=0.897 (0.859-0.933); External validation—AUROC=0.816 (0.773-0.857), Sensitivity=0.746 (0.591-0.903), Specificity=0.746 (0.575-0.929), PPV=0.653 (0.530-0.777), NPV=0.837 (0.762-0.915). Additional reported metrics: zero-shot AUROC=0.657 (0.598-0.702); temporal consistency Δs_ti=1.288×10^-1 and Δs_tr=2.495×10^-1

title: Multimodal Breast MRI Language-Image Pretraining (MLIP): An Exploration of a Breast MRI Foundation Model
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper tackles the lack of structured annotations and breast-MRI-specific foundation models by learning joint representations from breast MRI volumes and paired radiology reports. The goal was to build MLIP, a multimodal language-image pretraining model that supports clinically relevant MRI retrieval and downstream BI-RADS prediction. Its novelty is a CLIP-style framework adapted to 3D breast MRI, using a 3D ResNet50 image encoder and a radiology-specific RadioLOGIC text encoder; the authors position it as an initial exploration of a breast MRI foundation model. The main takeaway from the full-text results is that the approach is feasible and promising for suspicious-case retrieval, but performance for density/BPE retrieval and BI-RADS agreement is still modest, indicating the need for larger multi-center data, cleaner supervision, and more region-focused modeling.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Netherlands Cancer Institute (NKI) breast MRI-report cohort (private, single-center): training set of 15,005 paired cases; validation set of 3,013 unprocessed / 1,704 processed pairs; test set of 738 unprocessed / 380 processed pairs for BI-RADS analyses; density test subset of 100 pairs; low-BPE test subset of 155 pairs
Baseline model/architecture: MLIP (proposed CLIP-style multimodal model; no separate external baseline reported): 3D ResNet50 image encoder + RadioLOGIC text encoder + separate projection heads mapped to a shared 256-dimensional embedding space; downstream evaluation used the pretrained model in zero-shot form and a fine-tuned version for BI-RADS prediction
Training Approach: Weakly supervised multimodal contrastive language-image pretraining on paired MRI-report data with bidirectional image-to-text and text-to-image loss; all parameters trainable; AdamW optimizer; 20 epochs; batch size=4; followed by zero-shot BI-RADS prediction and additional downstream fine-tuning for BI-RADS classification
Medical Modality: Breast DCE-MRI, including pre-contrast and subtraction images
Model input modality: image+text during pretraining (3D MRI volumes + radiology reports); image + text queries/prompts during retrieval and BI-RADS inference
Evaluation Metric & corresponding value: BI-RADS 4/5 retrieval: AUC=0.717 (95% CI 0.604-0.824), Sensitivity=0.500, Specificity=0.868 at similarity threshold 0.433; Dense-breast retrieval: AUC=0.640 (95% CI 0.538-0.740), Sensitivity=0.327, Specificity=0.938 at threshold 0.435; Low-BPE retrieval: AUC=0.601 (95% CI 0.505-0.698), Sensitivity=0.518, Specificity=0.667 at threshold 0.354; BI-RADS human-AI agreement: Gwet's AC1=0.18 (95% CI 0.10-0.26) for zero-shot and 0.23 (95% CI 0.15-0.30) after fine-tuning

title: MedFocusCLIP : Improving few shot classification in medical datasets using pixel wise attention
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot medical image classification, where standard CLIP-style prompting can miss subtle disease-specific cues and offers limited interpretability. The main goal is to improve low-data classification by guiding the model toward clinically relevant regions of interest. The novelty is MedFocusCLIP, which uses zero-shot SAM2 segmentation masks as pixel-wise visual prompts before CLIP encoding, then combines image and text representations for classification. Unlike prior work that depends more heavily on supervised fine-tuning or manual/domain-specific prompt design, the method uses SAM2-derived localization to focus attention without supervised segmentation labels. The main takeaway is that ROI-guided CLIP consistently improves performance over CLIP, CoOp, CoCoOp, and standard CNN/Transformer baselines across several medical imaging datasets, especially in few-shot settings.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: COVID-19 dataset (exact source name not reported; public/private not stated); Lung Disease dataset (exact source name not reported; public/private not stated); Brain Tumor dataset (exact source name not reported; public/private not stated); Breast Cancer dataset (exact source name not reported; public/private not stated)
Baseline model/architecture: MedFocusCLIP = SAM2-generated segmentation mask + CLIP image encoder (ViT backbone) + CLIP text encoder + multimodal fusion + classification head / linear probe; main comparators: CLIP, CoOp, CoCoOp, ResNet, Res2Net, ViT, Swin Transformer; ablations: SAM Adapter in place of SAM2, and Swin Transformer in place of CLIP
Training Approach: Few-shot supervised classification; SAM2 is used in zero-shot/inference mode to generate ROI masks; masked images and text prompts are processed by CLIP; the paper describes a composite loss L = λLc + (1−λ)Le (contrastive + cross-entropy); evaluation is performed with linear probing using logistic regression on frozen multimodal embeddings
Medical Phase (pre/post): diagnostic/non-surgical classification task; not framed as pre- or post-operative
Medical Modality: Multi-modal medical imaging (explicitly stated: X-ray, CT, MRI; exact modality-to-dataset mapping is not fully specified in the paper)
Model input modality: Image + text (medical image after SAM2 masking/segmentation + class-name or descriptive text prompt)

title: Multi-Distribution Mammogram Classification: Leveraging Clip for Enhanced Generalization Across Diverse Datasets
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper addresses poor cross-dataset generalization in mammogram classification, especially for CLIP-style vision-language models trained on small and heterogeneous mammography datasets. Its goal is to improve external-validation performance for 3-class mammogram classification (normal, benign, malignant) by training across multiple public datasets instead of treating them as a single homogeneous source. The main novelty is MDMC-CLIP, which preserves dataset identity during training through prompt enrichment, so the model learns both class-specific and dataset-specific patterns rather than only generic class prompts. The main takeaway is that combining multiple datasets with prompt enrichment improved zero-shot generalization on unseen datasets and outperformed six compared VLM baselines.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Inbreast (public; train/internal validation); MIAS (public; train/internal validation); VinDr-Mammo (public; train/internal validation); CMMD (public; external test); KAU-BCMD (public; external test)
Baseline model/architecture: MDMC-CLIP built on small-scale OpenAI CLIP (image encoder + Transformer text encoder); compared against S-OpenCLIP, L-OpenCLIP, BiomedCLIP, MedCLIP, PubMedCLIP, and MammoCLIP
Training Approach: Supervised fine-tuning of a pretrained CLIP using contrastive image-text learning with dataset-aware prompt enrichment; multi-dataset training where each dataset is treated as a distinct domain and class+dataset prompts are used (e.g., 9 prompts for 3 datasets x 3 classes); zero-shot external testing on unseen datasets via cosine similarity between image and text embeddings
Medical Modality: Mammography (breast X-ray; multi-dataset mammogram images)
Model input modality: Image + text (mammogram image plus enriched class/dataset text prompts)
Evaluation Metric & corresponding value: Top-1 accuracy: CMMD=45.28%; KAU-BCMD=78.54%; Average=61.91%. Prompt-enrichment ablation: without PE CMMD=40.95%, KAU-BCMD=62.70%; with PE CMMD=45.28%, KAU-BCMD=78.54%.

title: Mammo-CLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model to Enhance Data Efficiency and Robustness in Mammography
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper addresses the lack of large and diverse annotated mammography data that limits robust computer-aided diagnosis in breast cancer screening. The goal is to build a mammography-specific vision-language foundation model that learns from screening mammogram-report pairs and improves data efficiency, robustness, and interpretability for downstream classification and localization. Its main novelty is Mammo-CLIP, presented as the first vision-language model trained specifically on mammogram-report pairs, together with multi-view supervision, synthetic report generation from attribute-labeled mammograms, and a new attribution method called Mammo-FActOR for sentence-level attribute localization without bounding-box supervision. The main takeaway is that the learned representation transferred well to public VinDr and RSNA tasks, outperforming CLIP-style baselines in low-label settings and enabling weakly supervised localization, although the work is primarily a diagnostic/pre-treatment study rather than a direct surgical-planning system.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: UPMC screening mammogram-report pairs (private; pretraining; 13,829 patient-report pairs / 25,355 mammograms); VinDr-Mammo (public; image-attribute dataset used for synthetic-report augmentation plus downstream classification/localization); RSNA Breast Cancer Detection / RSNA-Mammo (public; downstream malignancy classification)
Baseline model/architecture: Main model: Mammo-CLIP with BioClinicalBERT text encoder and EfficientNet-B2 or EfficientNet-B5 image encoder (ImageNet initialized). Interpretability module: Mammo-FActOR, a lightweight MLP on frozen image encoder channels for attribute-aligned heatmaps. Baselines/comparators: CLIP-objective model with ResNet-50 initialized from CLIP weights and CLIP-objective model with EfficientNet-B5; supervised localization used RetinaNet on top of image features.

Medical Modality: Multi-modal: full-field digital mammography (CC and MLO views) + radiology report text
Model input modality: Image+text during pretraining and zero-shot inference; image-only for linear-probe/fine-tuned classification and RetinaNet localization; image+text sentence-level alignment for Mammo-FActOR
Evaluation Metric & corresponding value: Best reported results - VinDr classification (Mammo-CLIP EN-B5, UPMC+VinDr): calcification AUC ZS=0.62, LP10%=0.92, LP50%=0.94, LP100%=0.96, FT100%=0.98; mass AUC ZS=0.76, LP10%=0.80, LP50%=0.84, LP100%=0.86, FT100%=0.88; density accuracy ZS=0.15, LP10%=0.83, LP50%=0.86, LP100%=0.86, FT100%=0.88. RSNA malignancy AUC: ZS=0.60, FT10%=0.85, FT50%=0.90, FT100%=0.91, LP100%=0.79. Supervised localization on VinDr (mAP@IoU=0.5): calcification FT10%=0.10, FT50%=0.25, FT100%=0.35, frozen-encoder=0.17; mass FT10%=0.43, FT50%=0.54, FT100%=0.58, frozen-encoder=0.39. Weak localization with Mammo-FActOR (EN-B5): mass mAP at IoU threshold 0.25=0.45 and 0.50=0.37; calcification mAP at IoU threshold 0.25=0.25 and 0.50=0.17.

title: A pathology foundation model for cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper develops CHIEF, a pan-cancer pathology foundation model for weakly supervised analysis of H&E whole-slide images across diagnosis, biomarker prediction, and prognosis tasks. The goal was to overcome the limited cross-site generalizability of task-specific pathology AI by combining tile-level self-supervised pretraining with WSI-level weak supervision and anatomical-site text conditioning. Its main novelty is a two-stage pretraining strategy that fuses CTransPath image features with CLIP-derived organ-site embeddings and then adapts the foundation model to multiple downstream tasks. Using 60,530 training WSIs and external validation on 19,491 WSIs from 32 independent slide sets, CHIEF consistently outperformed strong MIL/pathology baselines for cancer detection, tumour-origin prediction, genomic-profile prediction, and survival modeling. This is not a generative-AI or breast-surgery-planning paper per se, but it is a clinically relevant pathology foundation-model study with indirect methodological relevance to cancer decision support.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Public or controlled-access: TCGA; GTEx; PAIP; PANDA; BCC; BCNB; ACROBAT; TOC; CPTAC (CCRCC, LUSC, PDA, CM, UCEC, HNSC, COAD, OV, GBM, LUAD, BRCA); DROID-Breast; Dataset-PT; Diagset-B; MUV; PLCO-BRCA; PLCO-COADREAD; PLCO-LUAD; PAIP2020 (request-based public); TissueNet (request-based public). Private institutional: YH-Breast; YH-Eso; YH-Colon; YH-Sto; YH-Cervix; YH-Endo; SMCH-Endo; SMCH-Cervix; CUCH-Sto; CUCH-Eso; CUCH-Colon; CUCH-Pros; DFCI-BRCA; DFCI-LUAD; BWH-RCC; HMS-LGG; HMS-GBM.

Training Approach: Two-stage pretraining: (1) self-supervised tile-level pretraining on about 15 million unlabeled pathology tiles using CTransPath; (2) weakly supervised WSI-level pretraining on 60,530 WSIs with slide-level labels, attention pooling, instance-level feature identification, WSI-level contrastive learning, and CLIP-based anatomical-site text embeddings. Tumour origin: held-out macro-accuracy=0.895; independent micro-averaged one-vs-rest AUROC=0.9853±0.0245. title: A clinical benchmark of public self-supervised pathology foundation models
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper benchmarks public self-supervised pathology foundation models on 22 clinically relevant slide-level tasks from three real-world health systems. The goal is to identify which public encoders generalize best to routine clinical pathology data and to understand what pretraining factors matter for downstream performance. The novelty is a multi-institutional benchmark built from standard hospital workflow data, a standardized frozen-encoder plus GMA evaluation pipeline, and analyses of model size, pretraining dataset size/composition, and inference cost. The main takeaway is that DINO/DINOv2-based pathology encoders outperform ImageNet and usually outperform CTransPath, but bigger models or bigger pretraining sets do not guarantee better results; dataset composition appears more important, especially for biomarker tasks.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Benchmark/evaluation datasets (all private/internal; benchmark data not publicly released): MSHS Breast Cancer Detection; MSHS Oral Cancer Detection; MSHS Bladder Cancer Detection; MSHS Kidney Cancer Detection; MSHS Thyroid Cancer Detection; MSHS DCIS Detection; MSHS Prostate Cancer Detection; MSHS Colo-rectal Cancer Detection; MSHS IBD Detection; MSHS Breast ER; MSHS Breast PR; MSHS Breast HER2; MSHS BioMe HRD; SUH Melanoma BRAF; SUH Melanoma NRAS; MSHS LUAD EGFR; MSKCC LUAD EGFR; MSKCC LUAD ALK; MSKCC LUAD STK11; MSKCC LUAD KRAS; MSKCC LUAD TP53; MSKCC NSCLC ICI response. Key encoders: UNI, Virchow, Prov-GigaPath, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, Phikon, Phikon-v2, CTransPath, plus in-house DINO ViT-small SP22M and DINO ViT-base SP85M; comparator baseline: ImageNet-pretrained truncated ResNet-50 (tRes50).

Tissue tiles were extracted at 20x, embedded by each encoder, and aggregated with GMA. Medical Phase (pre/post): Diagnosis/treatment-response (mostly diagnostic or pretreatment pathology tasks; includes one NSCLC immune-checkpoint-inhibitor response task)
Medical Modality: Digital histopathology whole-slide images, primarily H&E WSIs at 20x; downstream labels came from pathology diagnosis, IHC/FISH, NGS, BioMe genetics, and RECIST-based ICI response
Model input modality: Image-only (H&E tile images / slide embeddings; no text or tabular input to the model)
Evaluation Metric & corresponding value: Primary metric: validation AUC across 20 MCCV splits. Detection tasks: all models achieved AUC > 0.90; average detection AUC examples reported in the paper were H-optimus-0 = 0.980 and SP85M = 0.978. Biomarker tasks: average biomarker AUC examples were H-optimus-0 = 0.785 and UNI = 0.773. NSCLC ICI response was difficult, with UNI average AUC = 0.60 and other models near chance. Scaling analyses: model size vs downstream performance Pearson r = 0.055 (detection, p = 2.59e-2) and r = 0.091 (biomarker, p = 9.52e-6); pretraining dataset size showed weak/no strong correlation with downstream AUC.

title: Benchmarking pathology foundation models: Adaptation strategies and scenarios
Summary of the paper (highlighting novel: This paper benchmarks how pathology-specific foundation models transfer across diverse downstream histopathology tasks when datasets, scanners, institutions, labels, and task settings change. The main goal was to identify which adaptation strategies are most reliable across 20 publicly accessible pathology datasets, four pathology foundation models, four classification tasks, one WSI-level survival prediction task, and multiple few-shot transfer settings. Its novelty is a two-scenario benchmark—consistency assessment and flexibility assessment—that systematically compares linear probing, full/partial fine-tuning, LoRA-based PEFT, MIL aggregation for survival, and several few-shot learning methods rather than reporting single-dataset fine-tuning only. The main takeaway is that PEFT was usually the strongest adaptation strategy for standard classification, Baseline/Baseline++ were strongest in low-data few-shot transfer, UNI and Phikon were generally the strongest backbones, and survival performance remained highly dependent on the MIL head and domain shift.
Datasets names (also is public or privat: Downstream benchmark datasets used in this study (all public): PCam; BACH; BRACS; Unitopatho; Kather19; Kather16; CRC-TP; DigestPath; Chaoyang; PANDA; AGGC22; UBC; DHMC; TCGA-LUAD; CPTAC-LUAD; CPTAC-LSCC; KBSMC Colon I; KBSMC Colon II; KBSMC Gastric; LC25000; CPTAC-PDA. Pretraining corpora of evaluated foundation models: CTransPath on TCGA (public)+PAIP (public); Lunit on TCGA (public)+TULIP (private); Phikon on TCGA (public); UNI on Mass-100K (private).
Baseline model/architecture: Main compared pathology foundation models: CTransPath (CNN + Swin Transformer hybrid), Lunit (ViT-S), Phikon (ViT-B), UNI (ViT-L). Additional compared adaptation/aggregation baselines: supervised-from-scratch, linear probing, full fine-tuning, partial fine-tuning, LoRA-based PEFT; survival MIL heads CLAM-SB, DSMIL, TransMIL, DTFD-MIL; few-shot baselines KNN, MatchingNet, ProtoNet, MetaBaseline, DiffKendall, Baseline, Baseline++.

Classification used five settings: supervised-from-scratch, linear probing, full fine-tuning, partial fine-tuning (bottom 50% of layers updated), and LoRA-based PEFT (rank=8); images were resized to 224×224 and optimized with Adam using cross-entropy. WSI survival prediction used 5-fold cross-validation on TCGA-LUAD with MIL feature aggregators (CLAM-SB, DSMIL, TransMIL, DTFD-MIL).
